newsitem.title: USA: KCBT wheat ends firm after buy stops hit late.
newsitem.headline: KCBT wheat ends firm after buy stops hit late.

text.p: KCBT hard red winter wheat futures ended mostly higher as buy stops were triggered in the May contract in fast, late dealings, traders said.
Traders said buy stops were hit when the May contract broke through Tuesday's high at $4.17 per bushel.
"That ushered in... some short covering and fund buying," a KCBT trader said.

KCBT March wheat expired in thin trade at $4.30, down 12-1/2 cents on the day. Traders said a five-lot was offered at $4.55 toward the close, but there was no interest in buying it there and it finally traded down at $4.30.

Overall, KCBT wheat settled 12-1/2 cents lower to 9-3/4 cents higher, with May up 9-3/4 cents at $4.18-1/2 -- its highest close since Sept 10, 1996, when it settled at $4.31. July closed up 7-1/2 cents at $3.86-1/2.
KCBT wheat had drawn support early from commercial interest in the May and possible fund-related buying in July, traders said.

Traders said Benson-Quinn bought May late on the stops, picking up 1.5 million bushels. Wolcott Lincoln had been an earlier buyer of 1.6 million July. E. D. & F. Man International sold 1.3 million July and 900,000 May.
